```{r}
#| label: setup
#| context: setup
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(lubridate)

# Make the logo available to the live Shiny server.
addResourcePath("www", normalizePath("www"))

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

# Use this message when the selected filters leave no records.
empty_plot <- function() {
  plotly_empty() %>%
    layout(title = list(text = "No records match these inputs.", y = .5),
           xaxis = list(visible = FALSE), yaxis = list(visible = FALSE))
}

# The course template reads its Titanic data directly from the course website.
df <- read_csv("https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/titanic_final.csv") %>%
  drop_na(Age, Embarked) %>%
  mutate(Survived = factor(Survived, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
         Pclass = factor(Pclass, levels = 1:3, labels = c("First", "Second", "Third")),
         Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("female", "male"), labels = c("Female", "Male")),
         Embarked = factor(Embarked, levels = c("C", "Q", "S"),
                           labels = c("Cherbourg", "Queenstown", "Southampton")))
```

# Plots

## {.sidebar}

Choose how to group the passengers. Both plots update automatically.
The Data page shows the same included passengers; choosing a grouping does
not remove passengers.

```{r}
#| label: sidebar-inputs
selectInput("group", "Group passengers by",
            choices = c("Sex" = "Sex", "Passenger class" = "Pclass",
                        "Embarkation port" = "Embarked"))

textOutput("selection_note")
```

## Row

```{r}
#| label: plot-one-output
#| title: "Age by selected group"
#| fill: true
plotlyOutput("p1")
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-two-output
#| title: "Survival by selected group"
#| fill: true
plotlyOutput("p2")
```

# Data

```{r}
#| label: table-output
#| title: "Searchable data for the current selection"
#| fill: true
DTOutput("tbl")
```

# Data Notes

::: {.card title="Data and interpretation"}

This is the course's Titanic dataset, restricted to passengers with a
known age and embarkation port. The grouping dropdown changes how the
plots compare those passengers. Proportions are calculated within each
group. These comparisons describe this dataset and do not establish causes.

The artificial practice-date column in the course file is not used here.

**Source:** [Course Titanic data](https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/titanic_final.csv).

Run this file with **Run Document**, then publish it on Posit Connect Cloud.
The HTML produced during rendering requires the live Shiny server.

:::

```{r}
#| label: server
#| context: server
# The dropdown changes the grouping in both plots.
filtered <- reactive(df)

output$selection_note <- renderText({
  paste(format(nrow(filtered()), big.mark = ","), "passengers included")
})

# Plot 1: Compare recorded age distributions across the chosen groups.
output$p1 <- renderPlotly({
  req(input$group)
  p <- ggplot(filtered(), aes(x = Age, color = .data[[input$group]])) +
    geom_density(linewidth = 1) +
    labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Density", color = input$group)
  ggplotly(p)
})

# Plot 2: Show the survival proportions within each chosen group.
output$p2 <- renderPlotly({
  req(input$group)
  p <- ggplot(filtered(), aes(x = .data[[input$group]], fill = Survived)) +
    geom_bar(position = "fill") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "#E07A5F", "Yes" = "#3D7EA6")) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = input$group, y = "Proportion", fill = "Survived")
  ggplotly(p)
})

output$tbl <- renderDT({
  filtered() %>%
    select(Name, Sex, Age, Pclass, Embarked, Survived) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10, paging = TRUE, searching = TRUE,
                   dom = "lftip", scrollX = TRUE,
                   language = list(info = "Showing _START_ to _END_ of _TOTAL_ records",
                                   infoFiltered = "(filtered from _MAX_ total records)")))
}, server = TRUE)
```
